A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SageAttention2 and provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures. All 19 pages of v2 and 20 pages of v4 were inspected, including v4's Appendix A. Material relocated from v2 can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V2 reports original kernel benchmarks, end-to-end model evaluations, and quantization ablations, including Figures 8–11 and Tables 10–13.

after.justification: V4 retains original experimental results and adds Hopper GPU comparisons, FlashAttention3-FP8 evaluations, and long-context results in the appendices.

M1.justification: V2's Equation 4 and Algorithm 1 use a sequence-wide Q mean before tiling; v4's Equation 2 and Algorithm 1 use a separate mean and correction for each query block. This revises one component of the retained quantized-attention procedure. Two-level accumulation describes the existing FP32-buffer strategy.

E1.justification: V4 extends existing long-context coverage with InfiniBench, including summarization, QA, code debugging, mathematical search, and retrieval tasks (Appendix A.7, Table 14). The original language, image/video generation, image classification, and Needle-in-a-Haystack coverage remains.

E2.justification: V2 cites FlashAttention3 without evaluating it. V4 adds FlashAttn3-fp8 to the CogvideoX-1.5, HunyuanVideo, and Mochi comparisons in Table 2 and to long-context comparisons. Hopper kernel plots also evaluate FlashAttention3 in FP16 and FP8. This introduces a directly relevant competing attention implementation.

E3.justification: V4 adds H100/H20 kernel measurements and evaluates Llama-3-262k (8B) up to 262k tokens on H100, extending the existing context-length/needle-depth evaluation. Original head dimensions, causal/noncausal configurations, benchmark metrics, and end-to-end latency settings are retained.

E4.justification: Table 18 adds component-overhead profiling beyond v2's single smoothing-overhead estimate. V4 also extends NIAH robustness comparisons to longer contexts with FlashAttn3-fp8 and adds its video failure examples in Figure 8. Existing smoothing, quantization-granularity, datatype, and optional V-smoothing ablations largely remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, run-to-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Retained averages and worst cases across layers summarize quantization accuracy rather than uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: V4 adds Hopper timings, FlashAttn3-fp8 video scores, component-overhead results, and long-context outcomes. Table 14 newly reports InfiniBench averages of 43.05 for full precision, 41.53 for FlashAttn3-fp8, and 43.06 for SageAttention2. Most existing end-to-end values remain unchanged; v4 Table 5 omits v2 Table 1's CogvideoX VQA-a column.

T1.justification: V4 Section 3.1 replaces v2 Equation 4's abbreviated smoothed-product equality with an explicit expansion containing a row-constant bias and explains why softmax permits discarding it. It also defines block-specific Q means. These are limited mathematical revisions; the per-thread formulas and accumulation principle largely remain.

C1.justification: V2 leaves Hopper implementation to future work. V4's abstract, introduction, and conclusion add the substantive claim of matching FlashAttention3-FP8 speed on Hopper while achieving substantially higher accuracy. The original technique contributions and broad plug-and-play accuracy claims remain.

C2.justification: V4 newly explains why transferring outliers with SmoothQuant is ineffective when both Q and K contain outliers, and why numerous small softmax values favor floating-point over integer quantization (Sections 3.1 and 3.3). The conditional benefits and optional status of V smoothing are retained.

D1.justification: V4 adds details about fused preprocessing, on-chip correction, register accumulation, and the 128-by-64, four-warp quantization-group example in Appendix A.5. It also identifies the long-context checkpoint. CUDA implementation and code access remain, but v2's Ubuntu 22.04 environment disclosure is omitted.

R1.justification: V4 adds CUTLASS, DeepSeek-V3, and InfiniBench references. Section 3.4 acknowledges earlier two-level accumulation for linear layers and locates the claimed novelty in attention. Positioning against FlashAttention3-FP8 becomes explicit, while most existing literature coverage remains; numerous publication updates are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: The preliminaries and method explanations are substantially rewritten and reorganized. FP8 quantization receives a dedicated subsection, while detailed per-thread formulas, dataset/metric descriptions, optional V-smoothing discussion, and several experiments move into Appendix A. Terminology and kernel names are standardized.

P2.justification: V4 adopts a two-column main layout, repartitions large benchmark tables between the main text and appendices, relocates many displays, and rearranges distribution plots. It adds Hopper charts, FlashAttention3 video comparisons, and a memory-layout diagram, while removing v2's standalone naive-INT4 video illustration.

improvement.justification: V4 resolves v2's explicitly deferred Hopper evaluation and missing direct FlashAttention3-FP8 comparison, substantially strengthening its practical speed-and-accuracy evidence. Longer-context testing and the more explicit smoothing derivation further improve support and clarity. These gains outweigh the limited loss of one ablation metric and the operating-system disclosure; most earlier experimental evidence is preserved.
